  exists recovery and streaming read only it. A later append, rotation or
  compaction transparently finishes an interrupted cleanup. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write failure.
- `weighted_batcher.resume_metrics(path, position=0)` streams records from
  `position` onward, where `position` is the number of records already read
  from the start of the segment set in write order. The position needs no
  conversion across appends, rotations, compactions, prunes or crash
  cleanup, and is only out of range when it exceeds the record total
  (pruned records included); equal to the total the stream is empty.
  Reading stays line by line and linear, never materialising the segment
  set. Raises `TypeError` if `position` is not an integer (booleans do not
  count), `ValueError` for a negative or out-of-range position (the latter
  while iterating), with the same path and line-level errors as
  `iter_metrics`.
- `weighted_batcher.prune_metrics(path, quota)` keeps at most `quota`
  records, dropping whole records from the oldest end in write order;
  `quota` 0 drops every record, and a quota at or above the current count
  removes nothing. A record is never split, empty and torn-tail-only
  segments spend no quota, and survivors keep their bytes, order,
  newlines, `-0.0`, oversized counters and key order. The set remembers
  the number of records pruned (`path.prune`), so pruned records keep
  their write-order ordinals for `resume_metrics`. Whole evicted segments
  are deleted and only the single boundary segment is rewritten, staged
  atomically at `path.trim`; a crash leaves either the old set or a set
  pruned to a complete record boundary, and a half-finished trim never
  joins recovery. Pruning is serialised with appends, rotations and
  compactions, and an unfinished compaction is settled first. Raises
  `TypeError` if `quota` is not an integer (booleans do not count),
  `ValueError` for a negative quota, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is
  missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a
  non-string path or a locking/write failure. Old segment sets with no
  prune marker need no migration; the first prune starts at zero pruned.
- `weighted_batcher.snapshot_metrics(path) -> str` pins the complete
  record sequence as of the call and returns a persistable snapshot
  handle. The pinned records are copied byte for byte into a
  snapshot-private file, so no later append, rotation, compaction or
  prune changes what the snapshot reads — the records survive even a
  quota-0 prune, and a compaction rewriting the segment members leaves
  the creation-time bytes (original newlines, `-0.0`, oversized
  counters, key order) untouched. Snapshots are independent of each
  other. A crash mid-creation leaves no usable handle behind, and the
  orphaned copy is removed transparently by the next write. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write
  failure.
- `weighted_batcher.release_metrics(path, handle) -> None` releases a
  snapshot handle and deletes its private copy. Reading or releasing the
  handle afterwards raises `ValueError`, as does a forged handle or one
  belonging to another segment set. Raises `TypeError` if `handle` is
  not a string, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing,
  `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a non-string
  path or a locking/write failure.
- `weighted_batcher.resume_snapshot_metrics(path, handle, position=0)`
  streams the records pinned for `handle` from `position` onward, with
  the same write-order ordinals as `resume_metrics`: records pruned
  before the snapshot still occupy their ordinals, a position inside
  that pruned region starts at the oldest record the snapshot holds, and

1	"""Durable append-only metric log with rotation, compaction, pruning and resume.
2	
3	Each metric occupies exactly one newline-terminated JSON line.  A record is
4	appended with :func:`os.write` against a single ``O_APPEND`` file
5	descriptor, so concurrent appending processes never interleave one line
6	with another.  Recovery acknowledges only newline-terminated lines: a
7	record torn by a mid-write crash survives as an unterminated tail and is
8	silently discarded.
9	
10	:func:`rotate_metrics` seals the current log into a numbered segment
11	(``path.1``, ``path.2``, ...) and leaves an empty log behind.  Segment
12	numbers are one past the highest number ever used, so deleting a segment
13	from the outside never makes its number come back.  Recovery walks the
14	segments in ascending order followed by the current log, so a record
15	accepted before a rotation never crosses a segment boundary.
16	:func:`iter_metrics` performs the same walk as a line-by-line generator,
17	never loading the segment set into memory.
18	
19	:func:`compact_metrics` merges every segment and the current log into the
20	single fixed segment ``path.1`` and leaves an empty current log.  Records
21	are copied byte for byte, still newline terminated, without re-rendering.
22	The merge lands first in a staging file at ``path.compact``; only after it
23	is fully on disk does cleanup begin.
24	
25	:func:`prune_metrics` enforces a retention quota by dropping whole records
26	from the oldest end.  Evicted records keep their write-order ordinal: the
27	segment set remembers how many records have been pruned in ``path.prune``,
28	and no operation renumbers surviving records.  :func:`resume_metrics`
29	resumes the same write-order walk at an integer read position; the
30	position needs no translation across appends, rotations, compactions,
31	pruning or crash cleanup.
32	
33	:func:`snapshot_metrics` pins the complete record sequence at creation
34	time into a snapshot-private copy (``path.snap.<handle>``) and records the
35	handle in the snapshot registry (``path.snapshots``), so later appends,
36	rotations, compactions and prunes never change what the snapshot reads.
37	:func:`resume_snapshot_metrics` streams a snapshot from a write-order
38	read position with the same ordinal rules as :func:`resume_metrics`, and
39	:func:`release_metrics` retires a handle and its private copy.  A copy
40	left behind by a crash before its handle was registered is not readable
41	and is removed transparently by the next write.
42	
43	:func:`snapshot_diff_metrics` reconciles two snapshots of one segment set
44	in write order -- the handle created first is the old side -- reporting
45	each extra record as ``added``, each vanished one as ``missing`` and each
46	byte-for-byte changed one as ``changed``, one JSON line per difference.
47	:func:`resume_snapshot_delta_metrics` pins the live record boundary the
48	way :func:`snapshot_metrics` pins a snapshot (a brief lock to settle and
49	capture the members, then a lock-free copy) and streams the records past
50	a read position that the holder of an older snapshot handle has not read
51	yet.  A reconciliation is fully lock free, and an incremental pull holds
52	the write lock only for the constant-sized boundary pin -- never while
53	its records are produced -- so appends, rotations, compactions and
54	prunes proceed normally while either read runs.
55	
56	:func:`checkpoint_metrics` persists a reader's place in a caller-named
57	cursor file.  The cursor binds the write-order read position, the
58	snapshot handle the reader pulls through and that snapshot's record
59	boundary (its pruned count and record total); every advance replaces the
60	whole cursor atomically, so a crash between consuming and advancing
61	leaves either the old cursor or the new one, never a half-written file.
62	:func:`resume_checkpoint_metrics` reads that one file and streams the
63	pinned snapshot from the stored position with exactly the ordinal rules
64	of :func:`resume_snapshot_metrics`.  A cursor takes no log lock to write
65	and reads only the snapshot's private copy, so concurrent readers with
66	separate cursor files and same-process writers neither block nor lose
67	updates.
68	
69	Every data-file descriptor is released before a rename on platforms that
70	cannot rename open files (Windows), so sealing, compaction and pruning no
71	longer raise ``PermissionError`` there.
72	"""

137	def _segment_numbers(path):
138	    """Return the already-used segment numbers for ``path`` as a set.
139	
140	    Every non-numeric sidecar (``path.compact``, ``path.prune``,
141	    ``path.trim`` and their temporaries) is deliberately invisible here.
142	    """
143	    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
144	    prefix = os.path.basename(path) + "."
145	    numbers = set()
146	    try:
147	        names = os.listdir(directory or ".")
148	    except FileNotFoundError:
149	        return numbers
150	    for name in names:
151	        if name.startswith(prefix):
152	            suffix = name[len(prefix):]
153	            if suffix.isascii() and suffix.isdigit():
154	                numbers.add(int(suffix))
155	    return numbers

163	def _write_bytes(fd, payload):
164	    """Write all of ``payload`` to ``fd``, retrying short writes."""
165	    view = memoryview(payload)
166	    while view:
167	        written = os.write(fd, view)
168	        view = view[written:]

179	def _same_inode(fd, path):
180	    """True when ``fd`` still names the file currently found at ``path``.
181	
182	    A rotation can rename the file while we wait for its lock, leaving the
183	    descriptor aimed at a sealed segment.  A momentarily missing ``path``
184	    (rotation crashed before recreating it) also reports False, so an
185	    appender reopens and recreates the live log.
186	    """
187	    try:
188	        current = os.stat(path)
189	    except FileNotFoundError:
190	        return False
191	    held = os.fstat(fd)
192	    return (current.st_dev, current.st_ino) == (held.st_dev, held.st_ino)

195	def _open_locked(path, create):
196	    """Open the current log, take the exclusive lock, and follow rotation.
197	
198	    Waits for the inter-process lock and then re-checks that the
199	    descriptor still names the live inode: a rotation may have swapped the
200	    path to a fresh file while we waited.  When that happened the sealed
201	    descriptor is dropped and the call re-opens the new current log and
202	    takes its lock, so a record is never written into a segment and two
203	    rotations never pick the same segment number.
204	
205	    ``create`` determines whether a missing log is created (append) or
206	    reported (rotation, compaction, pruning).  A lock failure closes the
207	    descriptor and leaves nothing written.
208	
209	    On platforms without :mod:`fcntl` (Windows) there is no process lock;
210	    the descriptor is returned unlocked, and callers that rename the
211	    live path release every handle first -- Windows cannot rename an open
212	    file.
213	    """
214	    def _open():
215	        if create:
216	            return os.open(
217	                path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
218	            )
219	        return os.open(path, os.O_RDWR)
220	
221	    fd = _open()
222	    if fcntl is None:
223	        return fd
224	    try:
225	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
226	    except OSError:
227	        os.close(fd)
228	        raise
229	    while not _same_inode(fd, path):
230	        os.close(fd)
231	        fd = _open()
232	        try:
233	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
234	        except OSError:
235	            os.close(fd)
236	            raise
237	    return fd
238	
239	
240	def _mutation_lock(path, create):
241	    """Lock the segment set for a mutation, or just prove the log exists.
242	
243	    Returns the live-log lock fd on POSIX (caller closes it) or ``None``
244	    on platforms without :mod:`fcntl`, where the existence check has
245	    already closed its descriptor and no rename may happen with a handle
246	    still open.
247	    """
248	    fd = _open_locked(path, create)
249	    if fcntl is None:
250	        os.close(fd)
251	        return None
252	    return fd

255	def _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create):
256	    """Re-lock the live log when settling swapped its inode.
257	
258	    Finishing a crashed quota-zero prune replaces the live file, so the
259	    lock acquired before settling dangles on the replaced inode and the
260	    new live log would otherwise be unlocked for the rest of the
261	    operation.  Re-open and re-lock the settled path (the same
262	    follow-rotation loop :func:`_open_locked` uses), returning the new
263	    fd; ``None`` (a lock-less platform) is returned unchanged.
264	    """
265	    if fd is None:
266	        return None
267	    if _same_inode(fd, path):
268	        return fd
269	    os.close(fd)
270	    return _open_locked(path, create)

299	def _read_prune_state(path):
300	    """Return ``(pruned_count, plan)`` from the prune marker.
301	
302	    A finalised marker holds the decimal pruned-record count; a pending
303	    one holds the JSON plan dict written by :func:`prune_metrics`, in
304	    which case the count it carries is returned alongside the plan.  With
305	    no marker the result is ``(0, None)``.
306	    """
307	    try:
308	        fd = os.open(path + _PRUNE_SUFFIX, os.O_RDONLY)
309	    except FileNotFoundError:
310	        return 0, None
311	    try:
312	        raw = b""
313	        while True:
314	            chunk = os.read(fd, _READ_CHUNK)
315	            if not chunk:
316	                break
317	            raw += chunk
318	    finally:
319	        os.close(fd)
320	    data = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
321	    if isinstance(data, dict):
322	        return int(data["pruned"]), data
323	    return int(data), None

332	        os.fsync(fd)
333	    finally:

335	    os.replace(tmp, path + _PRUNE_SUFFIX)

341	    The registry is a JSON object ``{handle: {"pruned": n, "total": n}}``
342	    published atomically, so a read never observes a half-written one; a
343	    missing registry simply means no snapshots exist.

361	def _write_snapshot_registry(path, registry):
362	    """Atomically publish the snapshot registry and fsync it."""
363	    tmp = path + _REGISTRY_TMP_SUFFIX
364	    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666)
365	    try:
366	        payload = json.dumps(registry, separators=(",", ":"))

369	    finally:

374	def _finish_snapshot_orphans(path):
375	    """Remove snapshot copies no registered handle refers to.
376	
377	    A crash between staging a snapshot's private copy and publishing its
378	    handle leaves the copy unnamed by the registry; such a half-finished
379	    handle never participates in reads, and its copy is deleted here by
380	    the next write.  Copies of live handles are always kept, so a prune
381	    (even with quota zero) or a compaction never makes a pinned record
382	    silently disappear.
383	    """
384	    directory = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
385	    prefix = os.path.basename(path) + _SNAP_COPY_SUFFIX
386	    try:
387	        names = os.listdir(directory)
388	    except FileNotFoundError:
389	        return
390	    live = {prefix + handle for handle in _read_snapshot_registry(path)}
391	    for name in names:
392	        if name.startswith(prefix) and name not in live:
393	            _unlink_if_exists(os.path.join(directory, name))
394	    # An incremental-pull copy is anonymous from birth on Linux; only the
395	    # named-temp fallback on an O_TMPFILE-less filesystem can leave a
396	    # file behind if the process died in the create-to-unlink window.
397	    cursor_prefix = os.path.basename(path) + ".cursor."
398	    for name in names:
399	        if name.startswith(cursor_prefix):
400	            _unlink_if_exists(os.path.join(directory, name))
401	    _unlink_if_exists(path + _REGISTRY_TMP_SUFFIX)

404	def _finish_staged_prune(path):
405	    """Finish prune cleanup when a prune plan is present.
406	
407	    Called with the writer lock held, by :func:`prune_metrics` itself and
408	    by any append, rotation or compaction that finds a plan a crashed
409	    prune left behind.  The plan is the commit point: the trimmed boundary
410	    segment has already landed whole at ``path.trim``, so finishing is
411	    pure filesystem cleanup -- delete the evicted members, publish the
412	    trimmed boundary atomically, then finalise the marker to the pruned
413	    count.  Lock-free readers reconcile a half-finished plan themselves in
414	    :func:`_resolve_members`, so a crash at any point exposes either the
415	    old segment set or the fully pruned one, never a mixture.
416	    """
417	    marker = path + _PRUNE_SUFFIX
418	    if not os.path.exists(marker):
419	        # A trim left by a crash before the plan was published names no
420	        # committed state and is discarded.
421	        _unlink_if_exists(path + _TRIM_SUFFIX)
422	        _unlink_if_exists(path + _TRIM_TMP_SUFFIX)
423	        return
424	    _pruned, plan = _read_prune_state(path)
425	    if plan is None:
426	        # Finalised marker: only an unpublished trim could linger.
427	        _unlink_if_exists(path + _TRIM_SUFFIX)
428	        _unlink_if_exists(path + _TRIM_TMP_SUFFIX)
429	        return
430	    for label in plan.get("evict", ()):
431	        _unlink_if_exists(_label_member(label, path))
432	    target = plan.get("trim")
433	    trim = path + _TRIM_SUFFIX
434	    if target is not None and os.path.exists(trim):
435	        # The plan is only published once trim holds a complete whole
436	        # segment.  Replace (not unlink-then-rename) swaps the boundary
437	        # atomically and creates the live log in the quota-zero case.
438	        # No data-file handle is held open here on Windows; on POSIX the
439	        # caller's lock fd is allowed to dangle on the replaced inode.
440	        os.replace(trim, _label_member(target, path))
441	    _replace_marker(path, str(int(plan["pruned"])))

444	def _marker_observation(path):
445	    """One immutable description of the prune marker.
446	
447	    Returns the marker text as bytes (``b""`` when absent).  Two equal
448	    observations bracket a window in which no prune committed, so the
449	    directory listing taken between them belongs to that marker's world.
450	    """
451	    try:
452	        fd = os.open(path + _PRUNE_SUFFIX, os.O_RDONLY)
453	    except FileNotFoundError:
454	        return b""
455	    try:
456	        raw = b""
457	        while True:
458	            chunk = os.read(fd, _READ_CHUNK)
459	            if not chunk:
460	                break
461	            raw += chunk
462	    finally:
463	        os.close(fd)
464	    return raw

467	def _resolve_members(path):
468	    """Pick the member files and pruned count to read.
469	
470	    Returns ``(members, pruned)``.  Numbered segments come first in
471	    ascending order, followed by the current log when it exists; the
472	    pruned count is the number of records already gone from the oldest
473	    end.
474	
475	    Resolution is lock-free but crash- and commit-consistent: the prune
476	    marker is read before and after the directory is listed and the pair
477	    must match, otherwise a commit straddled the listing and the read
478	    resolves again.  Pruning commits in the order plan publication,
479	    filesystem cleanup, marker finalisation, so an unchanged marker
480	    brackets a directory state that marker reconciles to exactly one
481	    settled record sequence:
482	
483	    * A compaction's fully landed ``path.compact`` staging file, while
484	      present, alone is the segment set.
485	    * A pending prune plan: evicted members still on disk are ignored,
486	      and while the trimmed boundary waits at ``path.trim`` it stands in
487	      for the boundary member; once the boundary is published its staging
488	      name is gone and the finished member is read directly.
489	    """
490	    members = pruned = None
491	    before = _marker_observation(path)
492	    for _ in range(1000):
493	        members, pruned, after = _resolve_once(path, before)
494	        if after == before:
495	            return members, pruned
496	        before = after
497	    # Extremely contended: return the last self-consistent pair rather
498	    # than loop forever; the data it reads is itself whole.
499	    return members, pruned
500	
501	
502	def _resolve_once(path, marker_raw):
503	    """Resolve one directory state, returning it with the post-listing marker."""
504	    if marker_raw:
505	        data = json.loads(marker_raw.decode("utf-8"))
506	        pruned, plan = (
507	            (int(data["pruned"]), data) if isinstance(data, dict)
508	            else (int(data), None)
509	        )
510	    else:
511	        pruned, plan = 0, None
512	
513	    staging = _staging_path(path)
514	    if os.path.exists(staging):
515	        members = [staging]
516	    elif plan is None:
517	        members = [
518	            f"{path}.{number}" for number in sorted(_segment_numbers(path))
519	        ]
520	        if os.path.exists(path):
521	            members.append(path)
522	    else:
523	        evict = set(plan.get("evict", ()))
524	        target = plan.get("trim")
525	        trim = path + _TRIM_SUFFIX
526	        use_trim = target is not None and os.path.exists(trim)
527	        labels = sorted(_segment_numbers(path))
528	        # Include the live log when it exists, and also when a quota-zero
529	        # cleanup is an instant away from replacing it from its published
530	        # trim, so the committed (empty) set never momentarily vanishes.
531	        if os.path.exists(path) or (use_trim and target == _LIVE_LABEL):
532	            labels.append(_LIVE_LABEL)
533	        members = []
534	        for label in labels:
535	            if label in evict:
536	                continue
537	            if use_trim and label == target:
538	                members.append(trim)
539	            else:
540	                members.append(_label_member(label, path))
541	
542	    return members, pruned, _marker_observation(path)

545	def _iter_lines(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
546	    """Yield ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` for complete lines in one file.
547	
548	    Reading happens one fixed-size chunk at a time, so an arbitrarily long
549	    single line is streamed rather than requiring the whole file in
550	    memory (only that one line is ever held at once).  The final
551	    unterminated tail is a possible torn write and is never produced, so
552	    callers cannot mistake it for a complete line.
553	    """
554	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
555	    pending = b""
556	    lineno = 0
557	    try:
558	        while True:
559	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
560	            if not chunk:
561	                break
562	            pending += chunk
563	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
564	            for raw in complete:
565	                lineno += 1
566	                yield lineno, raw
567	    finally:
568	        os.close(fd)
569

571	def _parse_lined(lines, label):
572	    """Parse ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` complete lines into metrics."""
573	    for lineno, raw in lines:
574	        if not raw or raw == b"\r":
575	            # A bare newline or a CRLF blank line carries no record.
576	            continue
577	        try:
578	            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
579	            yield parse_metrics(text)
580	        except ValueError as exc:
581	            raise ValueError(
582	                f"invalid metrics in {label} at line {lineno}: {exc}"
583	            ) from exc
584

586	def _parse_file(path, label):
587	    """Stream one segment or the current log through the metrics parser."""
588	    yield from _parse_lined(_iter_lines(path), label)

591	def iter_metrics(path):
592	    """Yield metric records across the segments and the current log.
593	
594	    Segments ``path.1``, ``path.2``, ... are streamed first in ascending
595	    segment order, followed by the current log at ``path``.  Files are
596	    read line by line, so the segment set is never loaded into memory and
597	    a single line may be arbitrarily long.
598	
599	    When a compaction has staged its merged segment at ``path.compact``
600	    but has not finished cleanup, that staging file alone is read; a
601	    staging file left behind by a crashed compaction is ignored until
602	    another append, rotation or compaction finishes it.  A pending prune
603	    is reconciled the same way: only surviving records are yielded.
604	
605	    A torn unterminated tail at the end of any file is silently discarded;

652	def _iter_raw_file_records(copy_path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
653	    """Yield each complete record line's raw bytes with its newline.
654	
655	    The chunked walk mirrors :func:`_iter_lines`, but lines are never
656	    parsed or re-rendered: blank lines are skipped exactly as on read,
657	    the torn unterminated tail is dropped, and every other complete line
658	    comes back verbatim with ``\\n`` reattached, so byte-level content
659	    such as ``-0.0``, huge counters and key ordering survives untouched.
660	    """
661	    fd = os.open(copy_path, os.O_RDONLY)
662	    pending = b""
663	    try:
664	        while True:
665	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
666	            if not chunk:
667	                break
668	            pending += chunk
669	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
670	            for raw in complete:
671	                if raw and raw != b"\r":
672	                    yield raw + b"\n"
673	    finally:
674	        os.close(fd)

701	def _finish_staged_compact(path):
702	    """Finish compaction cleanup when a staging file is present.

705	    :func:`compact_metrics` and by any append, rotation, compaction or

707	    staging file only ever holds a whole fully landed segment, so
708	    finishing is pure filesystem cleanup.

711	    :func:`_resolve_members`) until the final step: old numbered
712	    segments are removed and the current log is emptied while reads
713	    still resolve to staging, and only then is staging renamed onto
714	    ``path.1``.  Every involved descriptor is closed first, so no handle

736	def rotate_metrics(path):
737	    """Seal the current log into a numbered segment and start a new one.
738	
739	    The segment is named ``path.N`` with ``N`` one greater than the
740	    greatest number already present (``path.1`` for the first rotation),
741	    so a segment that was deleted from the outside never hands its number
742	    back out; an empty log seals an empty segment.  Afterwards ``path``
743	    exists again as an empty file ready for appending.  Every record
744	    acknowledged by a write ends up either wholly in a segment or wholly
745	    in the current log, never split across two.
746	
747	    A crash after the rename but before the live file is recreated still
748	    leaves the sealed segment readable; the next appender recreates the
749	    live log.
750	
751	    Raises:
752	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
753	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
754	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, locking fails, or another OS
755	            error occurs while sealing.  Nothing is written when locking
756	            fails.
757	    """
758	    if not isinstance(path, str):
759	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
760	    if os.path.isdir(path):
761	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
762	
763	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=False)
764	    try:
765	        _finish_pending(path)
766	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
767	        used = _segment_numbers(path)
768	        number = (max(used) + 1) if used else 1
769	        segment = f"{path}.{number}"
770	        # POSIX: the rename happens while the lock fd is held (an open
771	        # file may be renamed); the lock makes appenders reopen the path
772	        # before writing.  Windows has no fd in hand at all, so the
773	        # PermissionError an open live log used to cause cannot happen.
774	        os.rename(path, segment)
775	        # Re-create an empty current log without O_TRUNC: an appender that
776	        # won the unlocked rename window on a lock-less platform may have
777	        # landed a record there first, and it belongs in the current log.
778	        new_fd = os.open(
779	            path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
780	        )
781	        os.close(new_fd)
782	    finally:
783	        if fd is not None:
784	            os.close(fd)

844	def compact_metrics(path):

860	    segment: a half-written file left by a crash never joins recovery

945	def prune_metrics(path, quota):
946	    """Retain at most ``quota`` records, dropping the oldest whole records.
947	
948	    ``quota`` is the maximum number of records kept in the segment set;
949	    when it already holds no more than ``quota`` records nothing is
950	    removed, and ``quota`` 0 drops every record.  Records are dropped in
951	    write order from the oldest end, one complete line at a time -- a
952	    record is never split.  Empty segments and segments holding only a
953	    torn tail spend no quota and are removed with the prefix ahead of
954	    them.  Surviving records move byte for byte: order, original
955	    newlines, ``-0.0``, oversized counters and key order are unchanged,
956	    and an overlong single line still counts as exactly one record.
957	
958	    Evicted records keep their write-order ordinals: the set remembers
959	    the total number pruned, so read positions never shift (see
960	    :func:`resume_metrics`).  Whole evicted segments are deleted; only
961	    the single segment the cut lands inside is rewritten, via a
962	    ``path.trim`` staging file and a JSON plan in ``path.prune``, so a
963	    crash leaves either the old set or a set pruned to a complete record
964	    boundary -- a half-finished trim never joins recovery.  Pruning is
965	    serialised with appends, rotations and compactions by the live-log
966	    lock, and an unfinished compaction is settled first; every accepted
967	    record is therefore either kept or dropped, never lost or duplicated.
968	
969	    Raises:
970	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
971	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
972	        TypeError: ``quota`` is not an integer (booleans do not count).
973	        ValueError: ``quota`` is negative.
974	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, or locking or writing the
975	            truncated segment fails.
976	    """
977	    if not isinstance(path, str):
978	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
979	    if isinstance(quota, bool) or not isinstance(quota, int):
980	        raise TypeError(
981	            f"retention quota must be an integer, got {type(quota).__name__}"
982	        )
983	    if quota < 0:
984	        raise ValueError("retention quota must not be negative")
985	    if os.path.isdir(path):
986	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
987	
988	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=False)
989	    try:
990	        _finish_pending(path)
991	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
992	
993	        members = _segment_members(path)
994	        # One streaming count pass (the same cheap line walk reads use)
995	        # locates the cut; only the single boundary member is rewritten.
996	        counts = [sum(1 for _ in _iter_raw_records(member))
997	                  for member in members]
998	        total = sum(counts)
999	        if total <= quota:
1000	            return
1001	        drop = total - quota
1002	
1003	        index = 0
1004	        cumulative = 0
1005	        while index < len(members) and drop >= cumulative + counts[index]:
1006	            cumulative += counts[index]
1007	            index += 1
1008	        if index < len(members):
1009	            boundary_index = index
1010	            skip = drop - cumulative
1011	        else:
1012	            # Every record lies inside the dropped prefix.  The live log
1013	            # is the last member and always exists, so it is the boundary
1014	            # and is rewritten empty; everything before it is deleted.
1015	            boundary_index = len(members) - 1
1016	            skip = counts[-1]
1017	        boundary = members[boundary_index]
1018	        evict = [
1019	            _member_label(name, path) for name in members[:boundary_index]
1020	        ]
1021	
1022	        pruned = _read_prune_state(path)[0] + drop
1023	        if skip:
1024	            _stage_trim(path, boundary, skip)
1025	            target = _member_label(boundary, path)
1026	        else:
1027	            # The cut lands exactly on a member boundary: that member is
1028	            # already the oldest survivor and needs no rewrite.
1029	            target = None
1030	        # Publishing the plan is the commit point; from here on readers
1031	        # reconcile to the committed set even if cleanup is interrupted.
1032	        plan = json.dumps(
1033	            {"pruned": pruned, "evict": evict, "trim": target},
1034	            separators=(",", ":"),
1035	        )
1036	        _replace_marker(path, plan)
1037	        _finish_staged_prune(path)
1038	    finally:
1039	        if fd is not None:
1040	            os.close(fd)

1053	    conversion across appends, rotations, compactions, prunes or crash
1054	    cleanup.

1057	    which includes pruned records; equal to the total the stream is
1058	    simply empty.  At every moment the stream equals the corresponding
1059	    ordinal slice of a fresh from-the-start recovery (the member set and
1060	    the pruned count are resolved together in one call).  Exactly like
1061	    :func:`iter_metrics`, reading is line by line and linear without
